feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/public-sector CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant platform/communications leadership. It reads polished and substantive, but impact is diluted by repetition, limited quantified outcomes beyond web traffic, and a slightly overpacked structure.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: progression at NACo is logical and credible, showing growth from coordinator to director-level responsibility.  
- Strong domain fit: public-sector communications, Drupal modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia, and AI search are consistently aligned.  
- Writing is generally clean and professional, with good use of specifics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve scannability and strengthen structure.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include impact on engagement, efficiency, adoption, campaign performance, cost savings, or team productivity.  
- Fix style consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation/bullet formatting is inconsistent across roles; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically uneven unless intentional branding. No major misspellings found, but “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—consider “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and sector focus, but it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals and slightly tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrasing like “building the platforms” with sharper action language: “leading” or “modernizing” enterprise digital platforms, governance, and content operations.
- Add a concrete scale cue from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Trim the list of functions to the most differentiating themes: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Built and scaled digital systems supporting 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, and 50+ internal publishers, with expertise spanning analytics infrastructure, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search experiences” is more specific.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating too many broad capability labels here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into sharper, less repetitive capability areas with more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases and keep structure parallel; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experiences” for clearer meaning.
- Consider “editorial operations” instead of “editorial systems” if you want to emphasize leadership and process, not just tools.
- Standardize style: either use “and” throughout or “&” throughout; avoid mixing styles across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary almost line for line.
- Several items also duplicate Topline Skills; consider trimming this block to 6 items or making it more executive-level.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in recent roles. Tighten wording, standardize style, and frame these as selected examples with clearer outcomes or scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Retitle as “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp line with parallel verb structure.
- Reduce overlap with work experience by emphasizing distinct deliverables: “AI legislative search,” “Drupal 10 campaign microsite,” “anniversary campaign + conference installation,” “recurring advocacy video series.”
- Standardize style and wording: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently; spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot.”
- If space allows, add one concrete result, audience, or scale metric to 1–2 projects for impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats throughout; vary with “Launched,” “Created,” or “Led” for stronger rhythm.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around scope, platform leadership, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate bullets around impact: combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet on enterprise communications operations.
- Add measurable signals where possible: size of web estate, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search/discovery improvements, or efficiency gains.
- Example rewrite:
- Lead digital platform and communications operations for a U.S. national membership organization, improving web governance, workflows, analytics, and cross-channel coordination.
- Build Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing resource hubs.
- Deliver CMS/front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Spearhead an AI-enabled search initiative focused on retrieval strategy, structured content, and improved content discovery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work are already echoed in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer carry detail.
- “Governance/usability/best practices” overlaps with the summary and core competencies; replace with specific operational outcomes.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from the earlier NACo positions. Lead with transformation, team/operational ownership, and measurable business impact.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, video output, production cost savings, reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, or governance compliance.
- Tighten phrasing by removing generic verbs like “strengthened” and “expanded”; use “built,” “standardized,” “centralized,” “launched,” or “reduced.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise ownership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video/programming language may duplicate older NACo roles; emphasize building the in-house studio as a leadership/infrastructure achievement.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to execution-level leadership and channel growth, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and role level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points: newsletters, advocacy video series, cross-team editorial planning, publishing workflow improvements.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: audience size, send frequency, video cadence, engagement lifts, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders supported.
- Example phrasing: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders” / “Produced a weekly advocacy video update that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is too close to the Director role’s opening.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects section.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior-level leadership rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder engagement
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Stakeholder engagement” or “Mission-driven communications” to sound more executive and less tactical.
- Keep each line parallel in structure; avoid mixing nouns (“strategy”) with activity phrases (“audience-focused content planning”) unless all bullets follow the same pattern.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable impact for experience bullets, not this skills section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization

- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, high-value platform strengths and execution themes rather than repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as grouped capabilities, e.g.: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here unless central to target roles; keep Drupal first, and consider removing jQuery.
- Use broader phrasing that reflects recent work impact: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Platform implementation for high-volume public-sector sites.”
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to recent experience: “Drupal for large public-facing platforms” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; Topline Skills should stay higher-level.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome language: “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace generic phrases with stronger business-facing wording: “KPI framework development,” “executive reporting,” “SEO and digital performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, user behavior and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and Technical + IT more tool-specific.
- “Leadership reporting” may overlap with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and with tool-level detail in Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities rather than generic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability summary: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera studio systems • Virtual event operations”

- This item repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” from Core Competencies almost verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize platforms tied to recent impact: “Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency/context instead of just names: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the content.
- If GitHub Pages was only lightly used, drop it and keep the list focused on enterprise-relevant systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills; keep one list shorter or use this section for tools only and Topline Skills for strategic capabilities.
- Drupal already appears repeatedly in recent experience, so avoid overloading this item with extra Drupal wording unless adding meaningful context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus toward execution tools, not broad coding basics: “Front-End & Technical Implementation.”
- Use cleaner, more current phrasing: “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”; keep “JavaScript” and drop version-style labels.
- Group by function for readability: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, replace one generic item with a stronger outcome-linked tool from recent work, e.g. “custom Drupal front-end implementation” or “search/retrieval integrations,” since this better supports current impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding similar language here unless this section is made more implementation-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve scanability: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” to better match the actual mix of platforms.
- If space allows, add one short qualifier tied to impact, e.g. “used to support cross-team planning, publishing workflows, and operational automation.”
- Drop the weakest/oldest tool if not current (likely Basecamp or Trello) to emphasize recent, relevant platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, prioritize true automation/workflow platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope via modifiers rather than full bullets: **enterprise email automation**, **member communications**, or **newsletter operations**
- Optional stronger version: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (email automation, member engagement, newsletter distribution)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding claims like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience.
- If Higher Logic was your primary NACo platform, consider whether listing Mailchimp adds value or just broadens the list without relevance.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item mostly repeats the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo achievement bullets. It would be stronger if framed more crisply around platforms plus analytical capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten and standardize the list: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding”
- Replace the generic “SEO” with “SEO analysis” or “search performance analysis” to sound more execution-focused.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI dashboarding” or “executive reporting dashboards” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, group by function for readability: “Analytics: GA4, BigQuery, Clarity | Reporting: Power BI, Looker Studio | Optimization: SEO analysis, A/B testing”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with Topline Skills [3]; consider keeping the broader category there and using this section only for tools/platforms.
- “Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure…” in the 2022–2024 role already carries the impact; avoid repeating outcome language here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and team-building impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as an early-career build role: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten scope and emphasize execution: web refresh, livestream production, weekly video series, and cross-channel workflow support.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social volume supported, or size/timeline of the website refresh.
- Suggested rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize publishing workflows across channels. Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/producing, not expanding.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; use lighter wording here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim broad phrases like “supporting organizational programs and policy work.”

Suggested edit:
- Lead with the clearest differentiator: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for county-focused programs and policy priorities at NACo.”
- Make the podcast launch the centerpiece: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten the multimedia line: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and research dissemination.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or content outputs delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on the podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only or framed more strategically.
